newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeris downplay Russian kill of Caspian oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Azeris downplay Russian kill of Caspian oil deal.

text.p: Azerbaijan played down official Russia's decision to annul a $1 billion commercial deal to develop a Caspian Sea oil field, saying on Friday a way could still be found to tap the disputed reserve.
President Haydar Aliyev, returning to Baku from an official visit to Washington, told reporters at the airport he was not troubled by the flap.
"This is not an instance worth worrying about," he said. "I suppose a solution to the situation will be found."

Russian President Boris Yeltsin, after statements by Russian state oil holding company Rosneft that it was pulling out of the Azeri-Russian deal, signed a decree on Thursday formally "cancelling" the preliminary agreement to tap the field.
Rosneft, Russian oil company LUKoil and Azerbaijan's state oil firm SOCAR had signed a preliminary deal on July 4 to develop the deposit, which is estimated to hold 50-80 million tonnes of oil.
The field, called Kyapaz by Azerbaijan and Serdar by Turkmenistan, is at the centre of a territorial dispute between the two countries, both of which say the deposit lies in their sector of the sea.
Aliyev said Azerbaijan had never denied the disputed status of the field.
"Azerbaijan has never denied that Kyapaz is an interstitial field, since it is located on the border between the Azeri and Turkmen sectors of the sea," he said.
Prime Minister Artur Rasizade called on Azerbaijan, Russia and Turkmenistan to pool their forces to tap the oil.

"The optimal solution to the situation that has arisen would be a tripartite agreement between Azerbaijan, Russia and Turkmenistan on joint development of this reserve," he said, also speaking at the airport.
LUKoil had said earlier it did not want the project dropped.
